DUCKLINGS IN A LINE: five ducklings waddle single-file across the farmyard bridge while the farm girl, holding a basket of fresh rolls, crouches down giggling as the last one trips over its own feet and bounces right back up

GOATS ON THE COTTAGE ROOF: two fluffy kid goats stand triumphantly on the thatched cottage roof, nibbling the edges, while the shepherd below waves her crook and tries very hard to look stern through her laughter

PIGLET IN THE MUD PUDDLE: a round piglet sits blissfully in the biggest puddle in the yard, splashing with both trotters, while the farm boy leans on his rake grinning, mud already dotting his boots and cheeks

KITTEN IN THE KNITTING BASKET: a tiny kitten curls fast asleep inside the herbalist's yarn basket, one paw draped over a ball of green wool, while the herbalist carefully tugs a single strand free with two careful fingers
CHICKS IN THE OLD BOOT: three fluffy chicks have claimed a large abandoned boot by the fence as their nest, poking their heads out in a row while a proud hen circles the boot clucking encouragement

DUCKLINGS AND THE WATERING CAN: the farm girl waters her sunflower bed while two ducklings waddle after the spout, beaks open, convinced the little stream of water is a personal treat delivered just for them

LAMB IN THE LAUNDRY: a small lamb has tangled itself happily in a freshly hung bedsheet, spinning slowly on the line, ears poking through, while the farm girl clutches another sheet to her chest laughing too hard to help

HEN WHO FOLLOWS: the farm boy gathers eggs from the nesting boxes one by one while the very hen who laid them trots faithfully at his heels, craning her neck to inspect each egg as it goes into the basket

BUNNY AND THE SEEDLING TRAY: a plump bunny sits square in the middle of the herbalist's seedling tray, ears flat with contentment, while the herbalist kneels beside it offering a tiny carrot as a gentle bribe to relocate
WARM LOAVES AND THE CALF: the baker sets a tray of golden loaves on the windowsill to cool and a curious calf stretches its long neck just close enough to breathe them in, eyes enormous with wonder
THE PIE ON THE SILL: grandma slides a steaming berry pie onto the cottage windowsill and a row of sparrows immediately lines up on the sill edge, each one leaning forward with great personal urgency

JAM JARS IN THE MORNING: the baker lines up little jam jars with painted fruit lids along the kitchen shelf while a striped kitten on the counter bats each jar gently with one paw to inspect it before allowing it to stay

THE MEADOW PICNIC: the shepherd spreads a checkered cloth in the clover and pours two cups of lemonade while three lambs immediately step onto the corners of the cloth and stand there looking very pleased with themselves
HOT COCOA BY THE HEARTH: grandpa wraps both hands around a mug of hot cocoa in the armchair while a puppy climbs into his lap, sits upright, and stares intensely at the mug as though placing an order

THE BERRY STALL: the flower seller arranges little cones of red berries on her market stall while a duckling on the counter rearranges one cone with its bill, apparently improving the display to its own satisfaction

THE DELIVERY BASKET: the baker balances a wide basket of wrapped goods for delivery while a fluffy bunny sits on top of the pile, ears up, absolutely certain it is the most important item in the basket

THE FLOWER SHOP: the flower seller ties ribbons around bouquets while a small goat inside the shop mouths the end of a long ribbon and walks backward very slowly, unravelling an entire bow with great concentration

NAPPING IN THE HAY: the farm boy is fast asleep in a pile of golden hay with three puppies piled on top of him, one chewing his bootlace gently, one asleep on his chest, one watching a butterfly with enormous focus

TEA ON THE PORCH: the herbalist sits in her porch rocker with a cup of chamomile tea, and a large orange cat climbs onto the railing opposite, sits very tall, and stares at the steam rising from the cup with deep suspicion

FEEDING DUCKS BY THE POND: grandma tosses bread crumbs from the pond bank while a dozen ducks surge forward in a cheerful chaos, one duckling climbing directly over two others to reach a particularly excellent crumb

BLOSSOM PETAL MORNING: petals drift down from the orchard trees and a lamb lifts its head to catch them with its tongue, spinning in small circles, while the shepherd tosses a handful of petals into the air to keep the game going

PUMPKIN HARVEST: the farm boy rolls a round pumpkin toward the barn while a piglet trots alongside it, nudging it with its snout every few steps as though helping steer, both of them very serious about the task

FIRST SOFT SNOWFALL: the farm girl holds out both palms to catch the first fat flakes while a fluffy calf beside her does the same thing with its nose, blinking as each snowflake lands and vanishes on the warm pink tip

ONE UMBRELLA IN THE RAIN: the innkeeper holds a wide striped umbrella low over herself and a large white goose who has pressed against her boots, the goose leaning its neck out now and then to snap at a raindrop with great purpose

SUN AFTER THE RAIN: the farm girl steps into the yard after a shower to find every duckling standing in its own little puddle of reflected gold light, wings spread wide, as if personally absorbing the sunshine back into the world
